summary: Omitted labeled arguments generate an unwitnessed computed-return TOP after local-module resolution
evidence: Native OCaml 5.3 fixture /tmp/arch-index-reviewer-label-qt01kV/label.ml defines M.f ~a ~b = if b > 0 then (fun c -> a + b + c) else (fun c -> c), then partial () = M.f ~b:1 2. The independently compiled UID probe reports body arity=2, supplied Some arguments=2, and Typedtree argument slots=3 (the omitted ~a is None). The new branch returns syntactic arity 2, but nargs at line 2150 is List.length args=3; line 2267 consequently emits a residual. Executed the current collector on the same CMT with the optional ownership context disabled and enabled: disabled emits only M.f/module_param/partial=true; enabled emits M.f/enumerated/partial=true plus *TOP*/callback_param/partial=false. The real candidate DB contains that extra MAY_TOP row. A fully supplied M.f ~a:3 ~b:1 2 control has supplied=3 and correctly needs its residual. A focused assertion requiring zero residuals for the omitted-label case fails exit 1 (1 !== 0). Thus the existing slot-count issue becomes a new observable precision regression in the changed qualified-head path, violating FR-007's syntactic-arity preservation and the witness rule requiring supplied arguments > body arity. The existing four native cases and all 34 fixed410 residuals pass, so they do not cover this case.
fix: Use actual supplied expression arguments (Some entries), rather than all Typedtree slots, for the new known-body saturation/overapplication decision. Preserve the partial head and add a native omitted-label regression with a fully supplied overapplication control; assert the residual count and pending partial metadata. Keep unrelated CFG behavior scoped separately.
